parties.label: DEFENDAN
names: Razif Ahmad Bin Zuber Ahmad Khan

judgments.catchwords: 1. At the heart of the present application lies a familiar tension in the conduct of litigation: on the one hand, a person who is reluctant to give evidence and, on the other, a party who considers that person's evidence necessary for the just determination of the dispute. The law recognises that a witness cannot always be left to decide for himself whether he will attend Court and give evidence. It therefore provides a mechanism by which his attendance may, where the requisite conditions are satisfied, be compelled. That mechanism is the subpoena process. 2. The present application concerns the limits of that process. The 5th Defendant, who is herself a party to these proceedings, seeks in Enclosure 233 to set aside a subpoena issued by the Plaintiff requiring her to attend Court to give evidence and to produce certain documents. The Plaintiff, on the other hand, maintains that the 5th Defendant is a material witness whose evidence should be available to the Court at trial. 3. The trial of the action has been fixed for March 2027. 4. The application is supported by the 5th Defendant's written submissions in Enclosure 239 and reply submissions in Enclosure 243. The Plaintiff's written submissions in opposition are contained in Enclosure 241, with the Plaintiff's reply submissions in Enclosure 245. 5. This Court has considered the Notice of Application, the affidavits filed by the parties, the pleadings and Issues to be Tried, the written submissions and reply submissions of the parties, and the authorities contained in the respective bundles.
judgments.judge: YA Dr Choong Yeow Choy

parties.label: PLAINTIF

judgments.catchwords: 1. The Plaintiff commenced this action against the Defendants. There is nothing unusual about a suit being filed. In the course of the proceedings, the 1st to 3rd Defendants succeeded in obtaining an order requiring the Plaintiff to furnish security for costs in the sum of RM80,000.00. That too, in itself, is nothing unusual. This was followed by the present application in Enclosure 34 by the Plaintiff for a stay of that order requiring the Plaintiff to furnish security for costs. Again, this is not an unusual application. The unusual feature of the present case lies in this. The order for security for costs was accompanied by an Unless Order, providing that the suit would be struck out if the security were not furnished within the prescribed period. More significantly, by the time the present application for a stay comes before this Court for hearing, that period has expired and the consequence stipulated by the Unless Order has already taken effect. 2. It is this sequence of events which gives rise to the difficulty in the present application. The Plaintiff filed Enclosure 34 before the time prescribed for furnishing the security had expired. However, no stay was obtained before that period expired and the Plaintiff did not furnish the security. The question which now arises is what relief, if any, remains available under Enclosure 34 when the application comes before this Court for determination after the consequence stipulated by the Unless Order has already taken effect. 3. This Court has considered the affidavits and written submissions filed by the Plaintiff and the 1st to 3rd Defendants, together with the authorities relied upon by both sides.
judgments.judge: YA Dr Choong Yeow Choy

judgments.title: TEOH SEW NGOH & ors v TEOH KHIAN GUAN
judgments.catchwords: 1. This is the Plaintiffs’ application in Enclosure 12 for discovery against the Defendant pursuant to Order 24 of the Rules of Court 2012. The parties are siblings, and the main dispute in these proceedings concerns the circumstances in which certain shares came to be registered in the Defendant’s name and whether he holds those shares on trust for the estate of their late mother. 2. The Plaintiffs seek discovery of various documents relating to the four companies concerned, the transfer of the disputed shares, the properties held by the said companies and the personal and/or joint bank accounts of the late Tan Sai Hong. 3. The documents sought include audited reports, management accounts, general ledgers, Forms 49, registers of members, share transfer forms, board and members’ resolutions, bank statements of the said companies, documents relating to the transfer of the properties and the personal and/or joint bank statements of the late Tan Sai Hong. 4. The Plaintiffs’ case is principally that the disputed shares were transferred or allotted to the Defendant through undue influence, dominion over the deceased, fraudulent calumny and/or in circumstances giving rise to non est factum. The Plaintiffs further allege that the Defendant holds the disputed shares on trust for the estate of the late Tan Sai Hong. 5. The Defendant disputes the Plaintiffs’ claim. He submits that the discovery sought is excessive and is not necessary for the fair disposal of the action or for saving costs. 6. Having considered the pleadings, affidavits and the written and oral submissions of the parties, this Court dismissed the application in Enclosure 12. These are the reasons for that decision.
judgments.judge: YA Dr Choong Yeow Choy

The Fifth Defendant contends that he owed the Plaintiffs no duty of care, as there was no contract, dealing or proximity between them. Meanwhile, the Plaintiffs contend that their claim against the Fifth Defendant is pleaded with sufficient particulars in negligence and breach of statutory duty, and that it raises triable issues. The Court found that there are material facts in dispute between the Plaintiffs and the Fifth Defendant which cannot be resolved on affidavit evidence and must be determined at trial. For these reasons, Enclosure 118 is dismissed with costs of RM5,000.00, subject to allocatur.

judgments.title: PUNCAK NIAGA CONSTRUCTION SDN. BHD. v TM TECHNOLOGY SERVICES SDN BHD
judgments.catchwords: The Plaintiffclaimed that its underground fibre optic cables and ducts were damaged by excavation works done by the defendants. The Sessions Court held the First Defendant liable. The First Defendant appealed on both liability and quantum, arguing mainly that the Second Defendant was an independent contractor, so the First Defendant owed no duty of care and could not be liable for its negligence. The High Court held that the duty was personal to the First Defendant as the main contractor engaged to do the work, and the Second Defendant was only doing work the First Defendant itself was contracted to do. The First Defendant therefore could not escape liability by blaming its sub-contractor, and the finding on liability was affirmed. All the claims were disallowed for lack of supporting evidence or explanation except for one. The appeal was allowed in part, with no order as to costs.
judgments.judge: YA Dato' Raja Ahmad Mohzanuddin Shah bin Raja Mohzan

judgments.title: BELLWORTH DEVELOPMENTS SDN BHD v SETIAKON BUILDERS SDN BHD
judgments.catchwords: The Court of Appeal reaffirmed the principle of minimal judicial intervention in arbitration. A procedural breach, such as an alleged one-day delay in submitting a draft award for AIAC technical review, does not automatically invalidate an arbitral award where the requirement is merely directory, no timely objection was raised, and no prejudice is shown. An arbitral award will not be set aside on the basis of a purported “new difference” where the issue was within the parties’ pleadings, evidence and submissions. Courts will not review the merits of an award under the guise of a setting-aside application.’

judgments.catchwords: Pertuduhan asal di Mahkamah Tinggi ialah dua pertuduhan di bawah seksyen 39B(1)(a) Akta Dadah Berbahaya (ADB) - OKT Azril Sani dan OKT Aizad Imran telah dituduh bersama-sama - Di akhir kes Pembelaan, HMT telah melepaskan dan membebaskan OKT Aizad Imran daripada kedua-dua pertuduhan, manakala terhadap OKT Azril Sani, HMT telah meminda pertuduhan kepada seksyen 6 ADB dan seksyen 12(2) ADB masing-masing dihukum di bawah seksyen 39A(2) ADB - Di Mahkamah Rayuan, OKT Azril Sani merayu terhadap sabitan dan hukuman, manakala pihak Pendakwaan merayu terhadap keputusan HMT meminda pertuduhan asal terhadap OKT Azril Sani dan keputusan HMT yang melepaskan dan membebaskan OKT Aizad Imran - Isu sama ada HMT terkhilaf dalam membuat dapatan tiada perbuatan terangan atau “overt act” oleh kedua-dua Tertuduh dalam mengedar dadah itu sedangkan HMT telah menggunapakai anggapan perbuatan mengedar dadah di bawah seksyen 37(da)(vi) dan (xvi) ADB.
